info.title: Flightdeck REST API
info.description: The Flightdeck REST API lets a script or an app read and change work items, projects and their settings. Every request needs an API token, sent as a bearer token, and acts in the token's workspace. Lists are paged and come back as `{results, meta}`. Errors come back as `{error, code}`; branch on `code`. This document lists each endpoint and the exact fields it takes and returns. For what the fields mean and the rules behind them, read the help at https://flightdeck.example.com/help/api.

get.description: The projects you can read, by name. `query` finds one by name or identifier, best match first.

post.description: Needs a workspace member, admin or owner; a guest gets 403. The project gets the default states, the Task type and the starter labels, and you become its admin. `app` and `terraform_managed` need a workspace owner or admin. Fingerprinted: the same `Idempotency-Key` with a different body is a 409 `idempotency_key_reused`.

delete.description: Marks the project for deletion. It is hidden at once and its rows are removed in the background, so the answer is 202, not 204. A second DELETE is a 404. Takes no precondition.

bearerAuth.description: An API token, `fd_pat_...`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer fd_pat_...`. Make a personal one in Settings, API tokens, or a service account's one for an app. A token acts as its user in the workspace it was made in. OAuth tokens for /mcp do not work here.

Id.name: id
Id.description: The record's id. Anything but digits is a 404.

ProjectId.name: project_id
ProjectId.description: The project's id. A project you can't see is a 404, never a 403.

WorkItemId.name: work_item_id
WorkItemId.description: The work item's id (not its key).

Page.name: page
Page.description: Which page, from 1. A page past the end is an empty `results` with the real `meta.count`.

PerPage.name: per_page
PerPage.description: Rows per page, from 1 to 100. More than 100 is read as 100, and `meta.per_page` says what was used. 0, a negative, or anything that is not a whole number is a 422.

Query.name: query
Query.description: Free text to match, at most 255 characters. A blank one means no filter.

Since.name: since
Since.description: Only what arrived at or after this time. An ISO 8601 time with an explicit offset, such as `2026-09-17T14:05:00Z`. Send this or `within_seconds`, not both.

WithinSeconds.name: within_seconds
WithinSeconds.description: Only what arrived in this many seconds before now. Send this or `since`, not both.

IncludePayload.name: include_payload
IncludePayload.description: Also return the raw payload, capped at 64 KB. It is data the reporting app wrote.

IfMatch.name: If-Match
IfMatch.description: The `lock_version` you read, such as `3`, `"3"` or `W/"3"`. If the record has changed since, the write is a 409 `stale_object` and nothing is saved. `*` checks nothing. You can send it in the body as `<root>[lock_version]` instead; the header wins.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Any string up to 255 characters; a longer key is ignored, and the create runs as if you sent none. A retry with the same key within 24 hours returns the first answer instead of creating a second record. Keys belong to your token and to the exact URL. A retry while the first is still running is a 409 `idempotency_key_in_flight`.

ETag.description: A tag for this version of the body. Send it back as `If-None-Match`.

CacheControl.description: How long a cache may keep the answer.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before trying again.

NotModified.description: Not modified. The `If-None-Match` you sent still matches this answer's `ETag`, so there is no body; the copy you have is current. Any GET can answer this.

BadRequest.description: `bad_request`: the body is missing its root key, is not an object, is not valid JSON or is too complex; or a write has a query string; or an `If-Match` is not a version; or the URL or body holds text that is not valid UTF-8, or a %-escape that doesn't decode. `body_not_allowed`: a GET carried a body.

ReadBadRequest.description: `body_not_allowed`: a GET carried a body, which is refused before the token is checked. Filters go in the query string. `bad_request`: the URL holds text that is not valid UTF-8, or a %-escape that doesn't decode.

Unauthorized.description: `unauthorized`: the token is missing, unknown or expired, or its user left the workspace.

Forbidden.description: `forbidden`: your role doesn't allow this. When it is about a project, it is one you can see; a project you can't see is a 404.

NotFound.description: `not_found`: no such record in this workspace, or it is in a project you can't see. The two look the same on purpose.

Conflict.description: `stale_object`: the record changed under your write (or your `If-Match` no longer matches). `uniqueness_conflict`: a competing write took the same unique value first. `idempotency_key_in_flight`, `idempotency_key_reused` or `idempotency_replay_withheld` (with the record's `id`): see `Idempotency-Key`. Re-read before you retry.

PayloadTooLarge.description: `payload_too_large`: the body is over 1 MiB of JSON, or 4 MiB as a form. Nothing was read.

Unprocessable.description: `invalid_attribute`: the request named something that doesn't exist or can't be written (an unknown key, value or id, a read-only field, a bad page), or held a NUL character anywhere. Fix it rather than retry. `validation_failed`: the record's own checks refused it. Nothing was saved.

ReadUnprocessable.description: `invalid_attribute`: the URL holds a NUL character, which no id or filter can contain. Nothing was looked up.

ProjectUnprocessable.description: Nothing was saved. `app_taken` (another project already has that app), `invalid_attribute` (as for any write, a NUL anywhere included) or `validation_failed`.

RateLimited.description: `rate_limited`: more than 120 requests a minute for this token (or address, with no token).

DocumentRateLimited.description: `rate_limited`: more than 60 requests a minute from your address, whatever token you send.

comment.description: Keys other than these are ignored.

authored_at.description: When the comment was first written somewhere else, for an import. Needs the administer project capability, and can't be in the future. null or "" means now.

schema.description: The body goes under `sprint`, or under the old root `cycle`.
The body goes under `epic`, or under the old root `project_module`.

intake_item.description: Keys other than these are ignored.

submitter_name.description: Who asked, if it wasn't you. Free text.

submitter_email.description: How to reach who asked. Free text.

expires_at.description: When it stops working. Must be in the future. Leave it out, or send null or "", for a token that never expires.

project_id.description: A project in this workspace that you can see.

environment.description: The environment its errors are filed under. Defaults to "production".

incident_alert_rule.description: A new rule needs a name and an action that turns on at least one action.

reason.description: Why, in a few words. Shown with the hold.

github_integration.description: The secret can't change here, so a body that names `secret` is a 422.

Error.description: Every non-2xx answer. `error` is for people and may change; branch on `code`.

error.description: What went wrong. It repeats at most 100 characters of a value you sent.

id.description: Only with `idempotency_replay_withheld`, the record the first request made.

count.description: How many rows match, on every page.

LockVersion.description: Goes up each time the record changes. Send it back as `If-Match` (or `<root>[lock_version]`) to make a write fail if someone changed the record first.

code.description: A stable code for the reason.

Network.description: `public_project`: any member of the workspace can see it. `private_project`: only its members, plus workspace owners and admins.

IngestionTokenScope.description: `post_server_item` for a server app, `post_client_item` for a browser app.

AgentModel.description: An AI model an agent can run on.

StoredAgentModel.description: A model as it was saved. Usually one of AgentModel's, but a model that has since come off that list still reads back as it was saved, and you can send it back unchanged.

QueryBoolean.description: true or false. Anything else is a 422.

IdListQuery.description: One id, or several as `name[]=1&name[]=2`. A value that isn't a whole number is a 422.

WriteBoolean.description: true or false. Also the strings "true"/"false", "1"/"0", "t"/"f" and "on"/"off". null or "" means no opinion and leaves the value alone. Anything else is a 422.

StrictBoolean.description: true or false, as a JSON boolean. null or "" means no opinion. Anything else, the string "true" too, is a 422.

IdWrite.description: A record id: a whole number, or a string of digits. "7a" and -1 are a 422, and so is a number written with a decimal point, even 7.0, though JSON Schema counts 7.0 as an integer.

NullableIdWrite.description: A record id, or null or "" to clear it.

IdListWrite.description: A list of ids. It replaces the stored list; [], null or "" clears it. A null or "" in the list is skipped, and one id on its own is a list of one.

DateTimeWrite.description: An ISO 8601 time, or null or "" to leave it out.

DateWrite.description: An ISO 8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD. A time of day or a relative date is a 422.

NullableDateWrite.description: An ISO 8601 date, YYYY-MM-DD, or null or "" to clear it.

RichTextWrite.description: HTML, or plain text. Plain text becomes paragraphs.

PriorityWrite.description: A priority. null or "" leaves it alone.

LockVersionWrite.description: The `lock_version` you read, as a precondition. The same as an `If-Match` header, which wins when you send both. null or "" means no precondition.

PreconditionOnly.description: A DELETE's body may hold this precondition and nothing else.

ProjectFeatures.description: Every feature toggle with its effective value, defaults included. `self_healing` and `slack` are read only here: set them on the self-healing and Slack channel resources.

identifier.description: 1 to 10 uppercase letters or digits, unique in the workspace.

url.description: The project's page in the app.

github_repo_full_name.description: The GitHub repository this project maps to. Change it with a GitHub integration.

app.description: The deployed app this project stands for, by its cru-deploy name.

terraform_managed.description: True while Terraform owns the project's settings.

parent_id.description: The project this one is nested under.

Project.description: A project, in the list shape.

ProjectDetail.description: One project, with its shared links and Google files.

ProjectWrite.description: An unknown key is a 422. So is a read-only one (`id`, `url`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `github_repo_full_name`, `urls`, `google_files`), named with where it belongs.

identifier.description: 1 to 10 letters or digits. It is upcased for you.

archived.description: Read loosely, unlike the other true-or-false fields. null or "" leaves it alone. `false`, `0`, or the string "0", "f", "false" or "off" (or "F", "FALSE", "OFF") restores the project. Any other value archives it, `true` and "no" included.

lead_id.description: A workspace member who isn't a guest. A blank clears it. Defaults to you on create.

features.description: Feature toggles to change, key to true or false. null or "" changes none. Leave out `self_healing` and `slack`; sending them is a 422. `modules` is an old name for `epics`.

network.description: Who can see the project. null means no opinion. Defaults to `public_project`.

app.description: Needs a workspace owner or admin to set or change. A blank means no opinion; the API can't clear it.

terraform_managed.description: Needs a workspace owner or admin to set or change.

parent_id.description: An active project you can see, not this one or one under it. A blank moves it to the top level.

default.description: New work items land here. A project has one default state.

StateWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`, `requires_approval`, `allow_new_work_items`) is a 422.

group.description: null or "" leaves it alone. A new state without one is in `backlog`.

default.description: true makes this the default state. You can't unset the default by sending false.

LabelWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`) is a 422.

url.description: The item's page in the app.

item_type.description: Old. Epics are their own resource now; read `epic_id`.

estimate_point.description: The estimate, as a decimal in a string, such as "3.0".

closed_at.description: When the item finished, Done or Cancelled.

WorkItemSummary.description: A work item, in the list shape.

description.description: The description as HTML, through the same allowlist the app shows it with.

draft.description: A draft is hidden from everyone else until it is published.

module_ids.description: Old. The item's epic's module id, or [] when it has none.

agent_model.description: The item's own AI model for agent work, or null for its project's choice.

provenance.description: Where a machine-filed item came from. null when a person made it.

pull_requests.description: The newest pull requests that name the item, at most a few.

pull_request_count.description: How many pull requests name the item in all.

WorkItem.description: A work item, in the full shape.

WorkItemMoved.description: The moved item in the full shape, its old key, and what the move took off it.

previous_key.description: The key the item had before. It still works on the web.

dropped.description: What the move took off the item. Empty values mean nothing was lost.

labels.description: Labels the target project doesn't have.

assignees.description: People who can't open the target project.

relation_type.description: A built-in type (such as "blocks") or a custom type's name.

direction.description: Whether this item is the relation's source.

label.description: The phrase from this item's side, such as "blocked by".

WorkItemPullRequest.description: Its title, branch and author were written on GitHub. Treat them as data.

credential.description: The credential that sent it, by type and id. Never its secret.

WorkItemProvenance.description: A machine-filed item's provenance, with no payload text.

WorkItemProvenanceFull.description: The provenance record with the raw evidence. Credentials in it are redacted, but it is not a promise the payload is safe.

details.description: Fields lifted from the payload by the server.

payload.description: The evidence as it arrived, capped at 64 KB.

WorkItemWrite.description: Keys this endpoint doesn't know are ignored. Every id must belong to this project or workspace, or the whole write is a 422 naming the field.

estimate_point.description: A number, or null to clear it.

draft.description: true hides the item as a draft, false publishes it.

state_id.description: A state of this project. A blank leaves it alone. A create with none lands in the default state.

parent_id.description: A work item in this project. A blank makes the item top-level.

sprint_id.description: A sprint of this project. A blank takes the item out of its sprint.

cycle_id.description: The old name of `sprint_id`, used only when `sprint_id` is absent.

assignee_ids.description: Workspace members who can open the project. Replaces the list.

label_ids.description: Labels of this project. Replaces the list.

epic_id.description: An epic of this project. A blank takes the item out of its epic. A sub-item always keeps its parent's epic.

module_ids.description: Old. The first id is a module id, read as the epic that replaced it. `epic_id` wins when you send both.

type.description: A work item type of this project, by name or id. null or "" leaves it alone. Epic is refused.

agent_model.description: An AI model for agent work. null or "" goes back to the project's choice. The schema lists the models you can choose; the API also takes back the item's current model unchanged, even one that has come off the list, which a schema can't say.

created_at.description: When the item was really made, for an import. Needs the administer project capability. null or "" leaves it alone.

completed_at.description: When the item was really completed, for an import. Needs the administer project capability. null or "" leaves it alone.

closed_at.description: When the item was really closed, for an import. Needs the administer project capability. null or "" leaves it alone.

body.description: The comment as HTML, through the same allowlist the app shows it with.

authored_at.description: The time the thread shows. An import's own date, else `created_at`.

status.description: Worked out from today and the dates.

SprintSummary.description: A sprint, in the list shape.

Sprint.description: A sprint, with its description and progress.

SprintWrite.description: Keys this endpoint doesn't know are ignored.

start_date.description: A sprint's dates can't be cleared; null or "" leaves them alone.

end_date.description: A sprint's dates can't be cleared; null or "" leaves them alone.

EstimateRollup.description: The epic's work by state. In story points when every item has an estimate on a points project (`basis: points`), else in item counts (`basis: count`). `total` is completed plus started plus not started; cancelled is kept apart.

unestimated_count.description: Items with no estimate, on a points project.

legacy_module_id.description: The module this epic replaced, if any.

source_work_item_id.description: The Epic-type work item this epic replaced, if any.

EpicSummary.description: An epic, in the list shape.

description.description: The description as HTML, through the same allowlist the app shows it with.

LegacyModuleSummary.description: A converted epic in the list shape, with `id` as its module id.

LegacyModule.description: A converted epic, with `id` as its module id.

EpicWrite.description: Keys this endpoint doesn't know are ignored.

lead_id.description: A workspace member who can open the project. A blank clears it.

source.description: Where the request came from; `api` here.

kind.description: A person, or a service account.

id.description: The service account's user id, the one project members take as `user_id`.

name.description: The name the app shows for it.

ServiceAccountWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `role`, `joined_at`) is a 422.

email_address.description: On create, a new service account's address, or an existing one's to add it to this workspace. On an update, only the address it already has (or null or "") is accepted.

masked.description: A safe form to show, such as "fd_pat_…wxyz".

expires_at.description: null for a token that never expires.

ServiceAccountApiToken.description: A service account's API token. The secret is never here.

ServiceAccountApiTokenCreated.description: A new token, with its secret.

token.description: The secret, `fd_pat_...`. Shown only this once. null on a replay.

description.description: A blank one reads as null.

TeamspaceWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) is a 422.

lead_id.description: A workspace member. A blank clears it.

role.description: A built-in role (guest, commenter, member, admin), or a custom role's key.

builtin_role.description: The built-in role a custom role is based on, or the role itself.

ProjectMemberWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `name`, `email`, `builtin_role`) is a 422.

user_id.description: A workspace member. It can't change on an update; send the same one back, null or "", or leave it out.

role.description: A built-in role (guest, commenter, member, admin), or a custom role's key.

IngestionToken.description: An ingestion token. The secret is never here.

IngestionTokenCreated.description: A new token, with its secret.

token.description: The secret, `fd_post_...`. Shown only this once. null on a replay.

escalation_policy_id.description: Who gets paged. null pages nobody.

environment.description: The environment the key's monitor watches.

self_healing_trigger.description: Whether this key may trip the self-healing loop.

RoutingKey.description: A routing key. The secret is never here.

RoutingKeyCreated.description: A new key, with its secret.

routing_key.description: The secret, `fd_evt_...`. Shown only this once. null on a replay.

RoutingKeyWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key is a 422.

name.description: A blank leaves it alone. Defaults to "Routing key".

escalation_policy_id.description: An escalation policy in this workspace. null means page nobody.

self_healing_trigger.description: Whether the key may trip the self-healing loop. Can't change on a revoked key.

rollback_safe.description: true, false, or null when no verdict was given.

baseline_error_rate.description: Errors a minute before the deploy, frozen when the event was recorded. null means it couldn't be measured.

baseline_server_error_rate.description: The same, counting server errors only.

source.description: Which door wrote the row. Only `api_v1` rows steer the loop.

ReleaseEventWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key is a 422.

rollback_safe.description: true or false (also "true"/"false", "1"/"0", "t"/"f", "on"/"off"), or null to clear a stored verdict. Leave it out to keep the stored one.

deployed_at.description: An ISO 8601 time or date, at most 5 minutes ahead of the server clock. Defaults to now.

app.description: The app this release is of. The first event that names one sets the project's app.

actor.description: Who started the run. Shown, never acted on.

requested_by.description: The email of who asked for the deploy.

status.description: `not_computed` means the project was never checked.

production.description: The live release, or null when there is none.

release_candidate.description: The release candidate, or null when there is none.

days_behind.description: Whole days since the oldest waiting commit merged.

security_fixes_waiting.description: Dependabot alerts fixed after production's release, once production has one. `available: false` means the counts are null, never 0.

stale.description: True when the snapshot is old.

condition.description: When the rule fires. `count` and `window_minutes` read back as numbers.

action.description: What it does, as stored. Only the flags that are on are stored, so a flag you sent as false reads back absent. Read an absent flag as off.

actions.description: The action flags that are on, in order.

ErrorRuleWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`, `actions`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) is a 422.

condition.description: Replaces the stored condition whole. null or "" leaves it alone.

min_level.description: null or "" is the same as leaving it out.

action.description: Replaces the stored action whole, and must turn on at least one action, or the write is a 422. A false flag is the same as leaving it out. null or "" leaves it alone.

ErrorRuleAction.description: What the rule does. At least one flag must be true.

PriorityMap.description: Which work item priority each incident severity files at.

condition.description: When the rule fires. `count` and `window_minutes` read back as numbers.

action.description: What it does, as stored. Only the flags that are on are stored, and `priority_map` here holds only the rows that differ from the default.

actions.description: The action flags that are on, in order.

priority_map.description: The effective table, defaults included. Set it under `action.priority_map`.

IncidentRuleWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`, `actions`, `priority_map`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) is a 422.

condition.description: Replaces the stored condition whole. null or "" leaves it alone.

min_severity.description: null or "" is the same as leaving it out.

action.description: Replaces the stored action whole, and must turn on at least one action, or the write is a 422. A false flag is the same as leaving it out. null or "" leaves it alone.

IncidentRuleAction.description: What the rule does. At least one flag must be true.

priority_map.description: The severities whose priority differs from the default. null or "" is the same as leaving it out.

SlackEventFilter.description: Which kinds of change post to Slack.

slack_channel_available.description: Whether the workspace has Slack connected.

slack_scopes_sufficient.description: false until an admin authorizes Slack again with the channel scopes.

slack_channel_mode.description: null means link a channel with the name if there is one, else create it.

slack_notifications_enabled.description: false silences every Slack post for this project.

slack_provision_status.description: How setting up the channel went: queued, provisioning, linked, needs_invite or failed.

slack_invites_skipped.description: Members the last invite couldn't invite.

SlackChannelWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key is a 422.

slack_channel_mode.description: null or a blank means no change.

slack_event_filter.description: The kinds to change. null or "" changes none, and a blank value leaves that kind alone.

min_severity.description: The least severe incident that is sent to PagerDuty.

PagerdutyWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key is a 422.

routing_key.description: The PagerDuty Events API v2 integration key. Printable ASCII, no spaces. Never read back.

min_severity.description: Defaults to `error`. null sets it back to `error`, and leaving the key out keeps what is stored. "" is a 422.

project_id.description: The one project it covers, or null for every project.

Webhook.description: A webhook. The signing secret is never here.

WebhookCreated.description: A new webhook, with its signing secret.

secret.description: The HMAC signing secret. Shown only this once. null on a replay.

WebhookWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `workspace_id`, `secret`, `created_at`, `updated_at`) is a 422.

url.description: An http or https URL that gets each event.

events.description: The events it gets. null, "" or [] is none, and on an update clears the list. A "" in the list is skipped, and one event on its own is a list of one.

project_id.description: A project you can see, or null for every project.

WebhookEventWrite.description: An event. `module.created`, `module.updated` and `module.deleted` are old names, stored as the matching `epic.*` event.

SelfHealingConfig.description: The values the loop uses, defaults included.

armed.description: Read only. true when `rollback` is auto; change the mode with `rollback`.

count_browser_errors.description: Whether errors from a browser token count toward the trigger.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as "America/New_York".

PromoteWindowWrite.description: When auto-promote may promote. A part left out, or sent as null or "", keeps its value.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone, such as "America/New_York".

AutoPromoteStatus.description: The eligibility check's newest answer for the release candidate.

recent_errors_wait_off.description: null while it waits for a recent production error; else who turned that wait off.

feature_enabled.description: Whether the loop looks at this project at all.

rollback.description: `report` records what it would do; `auto` rolls back by itself.

rollback_blockers.description: What would stop auto-rollback acting in production right now. Empty when nothing would.

monitor_rollback.description: Whether a trusted monitor incident can trip the loop.

hotfix_incident_fixes.description: Whether a merged fix for an open incident starts a hotfix build.

auto_promote_status.description: null while auto-promote is off, or before its first check.

globally_disarmed.description: True while the server-wide switch stops every rollback.

overrides.description: Only the keys stored for this project, so you can tell what you set from what you inherited.

writable_settings.description: The keys a PATCH may send.

armed.description: Old. A change here is refused; send `rollback` instead. null or "" leaves it alone.

feature_enabled.description: Turning it on for a project stored as auto needs `rollback` in the same request.

rollback.description: null or a blank leaves it alone.

monitor_rollback.description: null or a blank leaves it alone.

auto_promote.description: null or a blank leaves it alone.

promote_window.description: The parts to change. The rest keep their value.

freeze_dates.description: Replaces the list. [] means no freeze dates.

id.description: null once the user is deleted.

candidate.description: The release candidate when the hold was set, or null.

promote_in_flight.description: A promote this hold came too late to stop, while it is still running.

AgentWorkModels.description: The AI model each kind of work asks for. A kind left out uses AutoPilot's default.

blockers.description: What would stop work being sent. Empty when nothing would.

lock_version.description: The settings row's own, 0 while there is no row.

AgentWorkWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key is a 422.

kinds.description: Replaces the list. [] clears it. null or "" leaves it alone.

models.description: Replaces the stored object. A kind left out, null or "" goes back to AutoPilot's default. null or "" for the whole object leaves it alone. The schema lists the models you can choose; the API also takes back a kind's stored model unchanged, even one that has come off the list, which a schema can't say.

label_id.description: A label of this project, or null for none.

research_label_id.description: A label of this project, or null for none.

agent_account_id.description: The service account work is assigned to, or null.

GithubCiFailureAction.description: What a failed workflow run on the default branch does.

ci_workflows.description: The workflows treated as CI, by name.

webhook_registered.description: True when Flightdeck added the repository webhook and will remove it on delete.

GithubIntegrationWrite.description: An unknown or read-only key (`id`, `project_id`, `webhook_hook_id`, `created_at`, `webhook_registered`) is a 422.

repo_full_name.description: owner/repo. It can't change on an update.

secret.description: Create only. Your own webhook signing secret, 16 characters or more. Never read back. Leave it out, or send null or "", and Flightdeck makes one and registers the webhook for you. On an update, sending it at all, null included, is a 422.

ci_failure_action.description: null or "" sets it back to `off`.

ci_workflows.description: The workflows that count as CI. Replaces the list; [] clears it. null or "" leaves it alone.

number.description: The group's number in its project, the "#42" people see.

url.description: The group's page in the app.

hashes.description: The group's identity, one or two rows.

suspect.description: Who may have caused it, from GitHub blame. Everything in it came from GitHub.

latest_occurrence.description: The newest sampled occurrence, or null once the sample has aged out.

recent_activity.description: The newest few changes to the group.

actor.description: Who did it, in the words the page shows.

source.description: A stable code for what did it, when no person did.

environments_truncated.description: Only when there are more than 100.

connecting_ip_hash.description: A keyed hash of the address the report came from. Never the address.

culprit_frame.description: The frame that threw, or null when there are no frames.

lineno.description: As the reporting app sent it.

colno.description: As the reporting app sent it.
